agent_returns.text:
Hand-off. I built two searches, both logged as in-flight.
- Chronicling America (Library of Congress): access `free_bot_protected`, log_006.
- Newspapers.com: access `subscription`, log_007. Your file lists only Ancestry, so this link may hit a login wall or a limited preview. Try the free one first.
- No plan item covers newspapers, so this is an ad-hoc search and no plan status changed.
- FamilySearch holds no newspaper collection for Schuylkill in 1908–09. It lists only church records and probate.
- Patrick Flynn's death year of 1908 is not disputed. The one conflict on file concerns his birthplace, so I left birthplace out of the search.
- Next: the researcher captures the results page. After that, a triage invocation lists the hits. Promising articles go to the record-structurer agent.

---

Open this search (free, from the Library of Congress digitized newspaper collection, limited to Pennsylvania papers from 1908 to 1909):
https://www.loc.gov/collections/chronicling-america/?dl=page&q=Patrick+Flynn+death&dates=1908%2F1909&fa=location_state:pennsylvania

It looks for a death notice or obituary for Patrick Flynn, which could name his wife, children, parents or siblings, and his burial place. Look for a Patrick Flynn who died in 1908 in Schuylkill County, around age 63. Watch for mentions of Pottsville, Shenandoah, Mahanoy City or other Schuylkill towns, and for any relatives named. Coverage is title by title, so finding nothing would not prove that no paper reported his death.

After the page loads, scroll to the bottom and back to the top. Press Cmd+P (Mac) or Ctrl+P (Windows), choose Save as PDF, and upload it here. Log in first if the page asks.

Second option, which probably needs a paid Newspapers.com account that is not on your file:
https://www.newspapers.com/search/results/?keyword=Patrick+Flynn+death&date-start=1908&date-end=1909&region=us-pa&county=Schuylkill

Capture it the same way if you can open it.

Once you upload the capture or captures, I will rate each article against what we know about Patrick and suggest which to examine closely.

output.text_response:
Hand-off. The site is MyHeritage, and the researcher has a subscription on file.

**Plan item pli_001 is now in_progress.** Log entry log_001 has been created.

---

**Open this search link on MyHeritage:**

👉 [Search MyHeritage for Josiah Barnes](https://www.myheritage.com/research?s=1&formId=master&formMode=1&useTranslation=1&exactSearch=&p=1&action=query&view_mode=card&qname=Name+fn.Josiah+fnmo.1+ln.Barnes+lnmsrs.false&qevents-event1=Event+et.birth+ey.1818&qevents=List)

This searches for **Josiah Barnes, born about 1818**, on MyHeritage. Look for a Josiah Barnes aged approximately 37 in Massachusetts, noting the town, county, and household members. MyHeritage ranks rather than filters results, so expect multiple hits — use the site's form to narrow by marriage year or parent names if needed.

**To capture results:**
1. After the page loads, scroll to the bottom and back to the top.
2. Press **Ctrl+P** (Windows) or **Cmd+P** (Mac) and choose **Save as PDF**.
3. Upload the PDF here: `https://genealogy.example.org/#/p/proj_7d4b2e91c6a05f38/upload`
4. Log in to MyHeritage first if prompted.

> **Note:** The same 1855 Massachusetts State Census is also available on FamilySearch, which can be searched via the `search-records` agent as an alternative.

Once you upload the capture, I'll triage the results and route strong matches to the record-structurer agent for extraction.

I made no plan-item update. The existing probate item (pli_006) names FamilySearch, not Ancestry, so it isn't this search.

- **Invocation:** hand-off.
- **Site and access:** Ancestry, collection "Pennsylvania, U.S., Wills and Probate Records, 1683-1993". The tool reports `access: subscription`. You have no subscriptions on file, so expect a login wall or a limited preview.
- **Log:** log_006, an in-flight entry. No capture has come back yet.
- **Date window:** the Ancestry link doesn't take a 1870-1890 window, so filter by date on the results page.
- **FamilySearch overlap:** FamilySearch holds "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683-1994", which is images only and not indexed by name. That is the collection pli_006 targets, and search-records or search-images can reach it.
- **Next:** capture the results page as a PDF and upload it, then I triage it.

---

Open this search:
https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/8800/?name=Thomas_Flynn&deathplace=Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States

I searched Ancestry's Pennsylvania wills and probate collection for Thomas Flynn with a Schuylkill County link. A will or estate file could name Patrick as his son, which would help identify Patrick's parents. Look for a Thomas Flynn who died in Schuylkill County between 1870 and 1890, and check whether the will or estate papers list heirs such as Patrick, Mary or James. After the page loads, scroll to the bottom and back to the top, press **Ctrl+P** (Windows), choose **Save as PDF**, and upload it here. Log in first if the page asks.

FamilySearch also holds its own Pennsylvania probate collection covering these years and can be searched without a subscription — just let me know if you'd like to try that route instead.

Once you upload the capture, I'll go through the results and rate which matches look right.

items.description: Patrick Flynn's birthplace: Ireland (1850 and 1860 censuses) vs. Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate)
items.independence_analysis: The two census records (1850, 1860) are independent original sources with different enumerators. The death certificate is a third independent original source. However, the census informants are likely the same household member (Thomas Flynn or wife), so the two census assertions may share a single informant — potentially not fully independent for this fact.
items.weighing_analysis: The census records are contemporary recordings made near the time of Patrick's birth, while the death certificate was created 63 years later. The census informant was likely a household member with firsthand knowledge (primary or indeterminate), while the death certificate informant (son-in-law) is clearly secondary for birth facts. Two contemporary sources outweigh one later recollection by a secondary informant.
items.resolution_rationale: Ireland is accepted as the birthplace. The 1908 death certificate birthplace of 'Pennsylvania' is rejected as a likely error by the son-in-law informant, who may have confused Patrick's place of residence with his place of birth, or may not have known Patrick was born in Ireland before immigrating as a young child.

These are index entries, so the original census page still needs to be found to confirm them.

Next, please open the Concord Josiah Barnes record on MyHeritage, save that page as a PDF and upload it, so it can be added as a source.
